answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonded collateral and cross-identity evidence: if k coordinated identities equivocate on conflicting statements, their correlated penalty scales quadratically, O(k^2), instead of linearly. Upon detection, the swarm’s capital loss receives an exponential multiplier, so adding aliases rapidly increases expected destruction of stake. Thus identities named terrace, thread, or nectar gain no safety from separation; shared control remains economically traceable and punishable.
